text:
sasha: quick follow-up from the RFC meeting — we need a compact decision on the probation/backoff boundary before the next rollout
pranav: agreed. main open question: should probation be enforced at the ingress proxy or at the central admission service?
anna: my vote is ingress for latency reasons, but central for global fairness signals. we might need a hybrid where ingress handles short-lived probation and central tracks longer term history.
mike: hybrid seems sensible. ingress can apply immediate short backoff (100ms-1s) and central can escalate to probation windows (minutes) with telemetry aggregation.
sasha: tradeoffs: ingress-only = faster enforcement but weaker cross-region coordination. central-only = higher tail latency on enforce path and more load on control plane.
lucy: another tradeoff: statefulness. If ingress keeps state, it needs sync/refresh for failover. central keeps canonical state but increases RTT on decision.
pranav: we can make ingress decisions mostly local using a short-lived token derived from central authority. e.g., central issues ephemeral probation tokens (TTL 30s) and ingress caches them.
anna: that matches what we discussed earlier for lease tokens. sketch of config I ran locally:```yaml
probation_policy:
  short_backoff_ms: 200
  short_backoff_max_ms: 2000
  probation_window_s: 300
  probation_threshold: 0.8 # abuse score
  token_ttl_s: 30
  grace_ratio: 0.1
```
anna: ingress would implement short_backoff_ms/short_backoff_max_ms and check cached tokens; central evaluates abuse_score over probation_window_s and issues tokens.
mike: telemetry: we need a compact signal set from ingress -> central: request_count, error_rate, rate_spike_ratio, token_violations. central computes abuse_score = weighted combination.
sasha: weights need experiments. initial proposal: abuse_score = 0.6*rate_spike + 0.3*error_rate + 0.1*token_violations. we should expose metric: security.probation.active_count and probation.escalations.{region,model}
pranav: canary plan: enable ingress short_backoff only for 10% of traffic in us-west for 24h, collect p95 latency and false-positive rehits.
lucy: also add a soft-fail mode where probation returns X-RateLimit header with remaining backoff instead of 429, so clients see guidance rather than hard fail.
anna: small implementation detail: eviction and probation expiry must be idempotent across restarts. central stores probation records in TTL DB (redis with sliding TTL).
mike: ops concern: central issuing tokens every 30s for many tenants could be heavy. we should batch issuance and give ingress leeway for tokens +/- jitter.
pranav: action items: 1) anna prototype ingress token cache and header format (due EOW) 2) lucy to draft metrics + alert thresholds 3) sasha to own canary rollout plan 4) mike to size central token issuance and batch strategies
sasha: +1 on owners. tiny UX note: include explanatory header X-Probation-State: short_backoff or probation_active and X-Probation-Score for debugging.
deploy-bot: canary feature flag (probation-shortbackoff) enabled for flag-bucket 'probation-canary-10pct' at 2026-03-21T14:07:02Z
lucy: can someone add the header names/semantics to the API observability page? I can PR once owners confirm.
pranav: one more: model fallback vs probation. if abuse_score high, should we reroute to cheaper model rather than block? saves availability. thoughts?
anna: prefer fallback for customer-facing routes, probation for admin or high-cost tenants. add flag allow_model_fallback boolean in policy.
mike: ok let's include allow_model_fallback default false and opt-in per tenant. that keeps safety first.
sasha: cool. if no objections I'll lock this design doc in a follow-up RFC summary and we'll start prototyping. :thumbsup:
pranav: no objections from me.
anna: good to go.
